title: Texas Republicans are scrambling after Bo French’s outburst
description: GOP operatives fear Bo French’s rhetoric could undermine the party’s recent gains with Hispanic and Asian American voters.
fullText:
Texas Republicans were already fretting about slipping support with voters of color. Then Bo French got on X.

The Republican nominee for Texas Railroad Commissioner posted a photo of a crowd of University of Texas football fans, most of them people of color, saying, "The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined." The Sunday morning comments, which appeared to target South Asian students, sent Lone Star Republicans into a frenzy, worried about the impact the rhetoric could have on GOP candidates up and down the ballot, including Attorney General Ken Paxton's high-profile Senate race and Texas Gov. Greg Abbott's reelection fight.

A number of Republican lawmakers, including some in tough races, quickly denounced the post as racist, as others squirmed with carefully worded statements. And GOP operatives winced at the potential electoral backlash — in a year that's already looking tougher-than-normal for a party that has dominated the state for decades. Still, no one explicitly called for him to drop out of the race.

"His post on social media is profoundly unhelpful if his goal is to see Republicans win statewide races in a tough political environment in 50 days," said Matt Mackowiak, an Austin-based GOP consultant who advised Sen. John Cornyn's (R-Texas) unsuccessful primary campaign against Paxton.

Cornyn condemned the post, asking whether other GOP officials would "condemn the intolerance and racism, or look the other way while it becomes normalized."

Rep. Monica De La Cruz (R-Texas), who is facing a tough reelection fight in a Hispanic-majority district, told POLITICO in a statement she's willing to "condemn racism" wherever it comes from.

"All I see in that photograph is a group of kids celebrating a Longhorns win. What can be more Texan than that?" De La Cruz said, before taking a shot at her Democratic opponent, Bobby Pulido, for his past racial comments.

And Karl Rove, a longtime adviser to former President George W. Bush, called French a "bigot" at a private lunch event and said he's voting for French's Democratic opponent, The Texas Tribune reported. Meanwhile, state Rep. Jon Rosenthal, the Democrat running against French, said he had his best fundraising day of the cycle after French's post.

French didn't respond to requests for comment. He repeatedly stood by his comments since Sunday morning. During a local radio appearance Monday, he said he didn't have any personal animosity against the students at the football game, but said that it is "not racist to point out that we should be favoring Texans over foreigners" and that his fellow Republicans are afraid of being called racist.

The divide emerging among Texas Republicans over the social media post — and Democrats' eagerness to capitalize on it — show just how precarious the party finds its position this cycle. Texas Republicans were already worrying about losing support from Hispanic and other minority voters amid a tough economic environment and President Donald Trump's unpopular immigration agenda. They need to hold onto or improve the incremental gains they made over previous cycles with voters of color in a fast-changing state where non-Hispanic white people now only make up 37% of the population. The stakes are high this cycle: Most polls show Paxton slightly trailing in a Senate race that could determine control of the upper chamber; Abbott appears to be in the toughest of his four election fights; and the state is home to several key House races.

"I don't think [French's post] independently and universally sours voter sentiment. But it contributes to GOP declining numbers with Hispanic voters particularly in the South Texas congressional races which we hope to win," said Alfredo Rodriguez, a Dallas-based Republican strategist, who called on French to "stop the petty political theatrics."

The blast radius of French's posts was wide enough to garner carefully worded responses from the top of the ticket. Abbott said in a Sunday statement that French's post "is not my message," before noting unity "doesn't mean that Texas cannot also lead in having the toughest immigration laws of any state in America and freezing H1B visas at our universities."

Two of the students in the photo told the Dallas Morning News that they're U.S. citizens. Most UT students are Texans — state law requires that 90% of each freshman class come from in-state — and there is no evidence that the students in the photo French posted are foreigners.

Some Republicans weren't thrilled about Abbott's response.

"This had nothing to do with illegal immigrants," said Anang Mittal, an Indian American national GOP strategist, of Abbott's comments. "These were students at a college game. They're not H-1B. If they're students, they're on a student visa. … It's pretty damn disgusting of Greg Abbott to say, 'I condemn racism, but also, like, we're keeping all the Indians out.' That's essentially what that tweet read to me."Democrat James Talarico called Paxton out on social media, asking if he would follow Cornyn's lead in denouncing French's post. The GOP nominee replied that he condemns "racism in all its forms" — and then claimed Talarico had a "history of dividing Texans by race."

Spokespeople for Paxton and Abbott did not respond to requests for comment.

Other Republicans were less willing to fully denounce French's comments.

"I don't really know the guy. I heard he said some not so pleasant things," said Rep. Troy Nehls (R-Texas), who said he hadn't seen the posts — but launched into a criticism of immigration nonetheless. "I am concerned about the number of people living in this country, and we don't even know who they really are," he said. "Shut the border down for 10 years, and then let's try to figure out who we got in this country because we don't even know."

Sen. Andy Kim (D-N.J.), who campaigned with Talarico in Houston on Sunday, said French's posts came up in conversations with every Asian American voter he met.

"Everyone was talking about it," Kim said. "Every single Asian American that I was with yesterday raised this with me. They were saying this is an example of, 'Not only are they not courting us or engaging with us, but they're actively demonizing us, actively being xenophobic and racist towards us.' We need leaders that stand up against this."

The political damage could also extend — potentially for years — to Texas' small but growing Indian American population, the demographic group French appeared to target in his posts. Both Dallas and Houston have significant Indian American populations. In 2019, an event at a Houston stadium headlined by Trump and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi drew over 50,000 attendees.

French's comments could alienate those same voters, said Brendan Steinhauser, a Republican consultant in Austin.

"He just irritated a bunch of people, many of whom could be supporters and could be Republicans," said Steinhauser, a University of Texas graduate. "I'd be willing to bet a lot of those kids that he was posting a photo of are probably, you know, their parents might be Republicans, or they might be Republicans, or conservatives, or independent-leaning conservatives."

If French is elected, he would sit on a commission that regulates Texas' powerful oil, gas and mining industries — which has little to do with immigration or social issues. But French, a longtime provocateur in Texas political circles, has a history of incendiary statements. Just last year, Republicans were calling on French to resign as chair of the Tarrant County Republican Party after he published an online poll asking whether Muslims or Jews were "the bigger threat to America." He deleted the post and said he regretted it, adding "antisemitism has no place in the Republican Party." This spring, he unseated a well-financed Republican incumbent for Texas Railroad Commission.

French isn't the only politician in Texas who has made singling out Muslims part of his political brand. Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick has made "preventing Shariah law in Texas" one of his legislative priorities. Patrick didn't respond to a request for comment. Abbott, Paxton and Cornyn have all called for investigations and other government action to stop development of a commercial and residential development being built by the East Plano Islamic Center, a mosque outside Dallas. And just last month, Abbott threatened to withhold funding from Dallas Fort Worth International Airport to block plans for ritual washing facilities for Muslim travelers in the airport's terminals. There's little difference between French's attacks and the other politicians' actions, said Yasir Qadhi, an Islamic scholar at the Islamic center."It is the same mindset," he said in an interview. "What we're witnessing is really an unprecedented and increasingly brazen form of racism. It's unfiltered, it's unapologetic, it's even stripped of even the pretense of political correctness. You know, this is a type of racism we've never seen in our lifetimes."

When French unleashed a string of inflammatory social media posts in 2025, several GOP officeholders — including Patrick, the lieutenant governor — called on him to resign as county GOP chair. But Republicans now refuse to tell French to drop out now "because that might mean that there would be a Democrat elected statewide," said Glen Whitley, a Republican former Tarrant County judge. "That's the bottom line."

"That's part of my frustration with the Republican Party altogether: They talk about being Christian, but they get up every morning to talk about who they hate," said Whitley, who still identifies as Republican but endorsed Talarico for Senate.

Joey Fox contributed to this report.

title: McDermott wants to commit to England for 2030 World Cup
description: Brian McDermott says he wants to stay on as England's head coach for the 2030 Rugby League World Cup.
fullText:
Brian McDermott says he wants to stay on as England's head coach for the 2030 Rugby League World Cup.

The former Leeds Rhinos head coach, 56, was appointed on a short-term agreement in April to guide England through this autumn's World Cup, which is taking place in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea.

McDermott said when he started in the job that he would be interested in staying on beyond the tournament.

And although he has made clear that he wants to focus on the immediate task of seeking success this October and November, he does want to commit to his country for the long term if all goes well.

He said: "Well, we've had a very informal discussion about what that might look like and then that's all it is. And it's been a really short conversation.

"Clearly, I'd like to do the job for longer. I'd like to get another crack at the World Cup in four years' time.

"You know, if you're going to do this properly, give me four years' preparation, where we're building it up year by year and getting players connected to a programme which has got a start, a middle and the end."

McDermott, currently working as an assistant coach at NRL club Gold Coast Titans, has taken the England role on a part-time basis, in contrast to his full-time predecessor Shaun Wane.

He has confirmed Wigan great Sean O'Loughlin and St Helens legend Paul Wellens as assistant coaches for the World Cup.

And he believes England are well set for it, but having had only a limited time to prepare - with no matches before their World Cup opener against Tonga in Perth on 17 October - he would like a chance to have a full build-up to a major tournament.

He said: "This has been a crazy, crazy period over the last few months to try and coordinate all this. And I think we're in good shape, by the way.

"But yeah, I've made it no secret. I'd like a crack at the next World Cup and a four-year build-up to that.

"We haven't gone too deep into those discussions. And when you mention it, you think, no, let's not talk about that. I've got to get my mind on this here. So it has been mentioned, but I'm not chasing that just yet."

New England boss McDermott offers route back for Connor

Rhinos dominate 2026 Super League Dream Team

McDermott said when he took the job that he intended to stick with George Williams as captain.

The Warrington half-back, who will leave Super League for NRL club Dolphins after the World Cup, returned to action in August after four months out with a neck injury.

Having got to know Williams during that time, McDermott is happy to have him leading the team.

"He's been great to speak to," McDermott said. "I didn't really know George at all.

"It's been really enjoyable to get to know him. He's keen as anything.

"And while he was injured, you could just tell he came back from injury early, but you could tell if there's anybody who's going to come back from it early, it would be him.

"And I'm really pleased to see the form that he's in now.

"His leadership's been really good. When we've had the groups meetings, I saw the way he would speak on there and just have a bit of maturity.

title: Wales lose injured Powell for entire WXV campaign
description: Wales have been dealt another injury blow ahead of their WXV Global Series with Kayleigh Powell ruled out of the entire campaign.
fullText:
Wales have been dealt another injury blow before their WXV Global Series campaign with Harlequins' Kayleigh Powell ruled out of the entire tournament.

The 27-year-old sevens Olympian was a standout player at full-back during the Six Nations and impressed at fly-half when Wales ended their nine match losing streak against the Barbarians in June.

But she will sit out Wales' Tests against South Africa, USA and Japan after suffering a hamstring injury in training.

Powell wrote on her social media that she was "absolutely gutted" to be missing the campaign, but has "every faith that this team will do great things."

Head coach Sean Lynn is already without Premiership Women's Rugby (PRW) title-winning prop Donna Rose, while backs Carys Cox and Nel Metcalfe have only just returned to training.

Lleucu George could slot back in at 10, while scrum-half Keira Bevan provides Lynn another option having trained there during pre-season.

Wales open their campaign against South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park on Friday (19:15 BST).

title: US acknowledges for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space
description: The United States has confirmed for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space.  Air Force Secretary Troy Meink told the Air and Space Cyber Conference in Maryland on Monday that the U.S. ha...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The United States has confirmed for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space.

Air Force Secretary Troy Meink told the Air and Space Cyber Conference in Maryland on Monday that the U.S. has fielded "on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action."

Meink did not detail what the weapons were or how they work. In 2024 the U.S. said Russia was developing a new anti-satellite weapon that could be launched from space. At the time the White House said the danger wasn't imminent.

But reports of the anti-satellite weapon reflected longstanding worries about space threats from Russia and China, given that much U.S. infrastructure is dependent on satellite communications.

In his remarks, Meink also said the Air Force was adding more autonomous systems to its capabilities and predicted the service would look "radically different" by 2032. For example, he foresaw one-way attack drones replacing artillery as the "primary killer."

"We are increasing readiness against existing threats," he said.

Trump created the Space Force in 2019.

title: The 'Brampton bagsman' taking Championship by storm
description: BBC Sport takes a look at the scintillating form of Southampton's 'Brampton bagsman' Cyle Larin.
fullText:
Not many forwards in world football have had a better start to their season than Southampton's Cyle Larin.

The Canada striker is the leading goalscorer in the Championship and has netted more than anyone in Europe's top five leagues.

He may have played more games than the stars from the Premier League and La Liga, but his seven goals in seven league matches have caught the eye.

His average of 73 minutes per goal is better than the 75 Kylian Mbappe is averaging for Real Madrid and Erling Haaland's 90 minutes per strike in the Premier League for Manchester City.

Larin's exploits have even led Saints head coach Tonda Eckert to label him "the best striker in the league" - lofty praise in a division that also boasts Jarrod Bowen, Raul Jimenez, Mohamed Toure and the emerging Will Lankshear.

But it is not just favouritism from his manager - neutral plaudits, including August's Championship Player of the Month award, are also landing at his feet.

The 'Brampton bagsman' - a nickname coined from his Ontario hometown - has helped propel Eckert's team from bottom of the table on minus four points to inside the top eight with 10.

Saints would be second, behind West Ham on goal difference, if not for the points deduction that came as punishment for the Spygate scandal.

But after a nomadic career that has taken in spells in the United States, Turkey, Belgium, Spain and the Netherlands, why has Larin been so effective for the south coast side?

Since signing for Southampton on an initial loan from Mallorca in early 2026, Larin's first venture into English football has been an impactful one.

The 31-year-old netted three minutes into his Saints debut last season, going on to finish with eight Championship goals in 16 games during the second half of the campaign.

Following the fall-out from Spygate, he did not get the chance to help Southampton reach the Premier League but had to quickly turn his attention to the World Cup and representing his country as one of the host nations.

He shone for Canada on the biggest of stages, scoring two goals - one a crucial late equaliser against Bosnia-Herzegovina - as Jesse Marsch's side reached the last 16 before losing to Morocco.

Larin's contribution for Canada as their second all-time leading goalscorer has even earned him a key to his home city of Brampton,, external something he will collect during the upcoming international break.

Back on English soil, Larin has been even more prolific for Saints than he was last term, scoring eight times in nine appearances across all competitions.

However, the forward has been quick to point out it has been far from a solo effort.

"It feels good but I don't think I can do this without my team-mates," he told BBC Radio Solent after scoring twice in the 4-1 win over Bristol City on Saturday.

"They play such a big role in me being able to score and I have to give credit to the coach too, he's given me the role to play free up there and that's what I'm doing.

"It's the beginning of the season and we have to keep working hard as we have a long way to go. You can't get too high after these games, you have to be level-headed."

Larin has a point - in Finn Azaz and Leo Scienza, who boast five goals and six assists between them already this term, he has two of the division's best creators a striker could wish for.

Eckert hails 'best in the league' Larin

Does Larin need more help up top?

Last season, he shared the minutes up front with Ross Stewart but with the Scot now at Swansea and Larin clearly the first choice at St Mary's, he has been taking advantage of more minutes on the pitch.

Larin rarely completes 90 minutes with Eckert tending to prefer to withdraw him during the second half - and that makes his statistics even more impressive.

He is averaging 1.23 goals per 90 minutes, scoring every 73 minutes with a goal conversion rate of 25% - seven goals from 28 shots.

Only one other striker - Norwich's Mathias Kvistgaarden (1.27) - has a better goal per 90 minutes rate and only Bowen (29) has attempted more shots.

"When you have quality footballers like Larin then you get goals," former Saints midfielder Jo Tessem said on the latest episode of BBC Radio Solent's Goin' Home.

"Quality players like him step up when you need them and so far this season he's done that.

"Eckert has said that Larin has been a lot fitter right now than when he arrived in January and that has made a difference so far."

There's a simplicity to Cyle Larin's game - and understanding that has underpinned Southampton's strong start to the campaign.

Rarely tasked with dropping into the build-up, he hangs on the opposition's last line, ready to make powerful runs into the channels.

Tonda Eckert has asked fans to trust Saints when they build from the back, with Larin's movement a significant reason why.

If his team-mates play through the press, he has the space to stretch defences and finish off swift counter attacks.

Larin has stressed the help of his team-mates too.

The immediacy of his runs creates the room for Azaz between the lines and for the combinations between the pair that preceded Larin's opening goal against Bristol City, for example.

Finding space in crowded situations, though - especially for a side who want to dominate possession - is equally crucial for a centre-forward.

Larin's instinctive movement and clever body usage offer a potent mix of snappy shots off either foot, aerial threat and those tricks of the trade the 31-year-old has picked up over the years.

A Larin trademark is drifting to the back post, a magnet for the crossing quality of right-back James Bree.

He is low touch, high impact - but that's just the system Eckert wants around his main man.

title: A team in form - how Farke has turned Leeds around
description: With Leeds United third in the Premier League, BBC Sport assesses their improvement under Daniel Farke.
fullText:
As the nascent Premier League table takes shape, the sight of Leeds United in third place feels like a throwback to the turn of the century, when they secured five top-five finishes on the bounce.

Monday's 4-1 home win over Newcastle United means Daniel Farke's unbeaten side have made their best start to a top-flight season since 2001-02 under David O'Leary.

In truth, Leeds, with eight points from four games, have been playing well for some time, and it can all be traced back to a bold change of formation by Farke almost nine months ago.

The German switched from a back four to a back three at half-time against Manchester City on 29 November, a game in which his team battled back from 2-0 down at the break to level things at 2-2 before conceding in stoppage time at Etihad Stadium.

Starting with the subsequent home win over Chelsea on 3 December, Leeds have lost only five of their past 29 league games, results which would place them fifth in the hypothetical league table for that timeframe.

So how have they done it? And can they push for European football for the first time in 24 years?

In the 2025 summer transfer window Farke and the club's new sporting director Adam Underwood made a point of signing tall players who could "add a special physicality" to the squad they were building for the robust demands of the English top flight.

Of the 10 permanent arrivals, eight – Jaka Bijol, Sebastiaan Bornauw, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, James Justin, Lukas Nmecha, Noah Okafor, Lucas Perri and Anton Stach – stand more than 6ft tall.

Speaking in July 2025, Farke said: "I wouldn't say it's coincidence that they are all tall players but, of course, if you join the Premier League and you have one of the smallest groups, you expect that probably there is more pressure on you than there was in the Championship. You have to make sure that you're also good in defending crosses."

This summer, after losing centre-back Pascal Struijk to Brighton, Farke moved for two World Cup players - Bosnia-Herzegovina's Tarik Muharemovic and Switzerland's Nico Elvedi - to bolster his defence.

Despite an error leading to Bazoumana Toure's late consolation goal for Newcastle, Muharemovic has looked particularly impressive, playing every league minute in front of 6ft 5in England international James Trafford, who became the most expensive British goalkeeper in history for the second time when he joined for an initial £40m from City.

Throw in Harry Wilson, one of the league's standout players last season, who joined on a free transfer from Fulham, and Leeds' latest signings look to be particularly shrewd.

Leeds lost eight of their first 13 league games in 2025-26, leaving them in 18th position and facing the very real prospect of relegation.

Reports at the time suggested Farke, whose side had pipped Burnley to the Championship title the previous season, was in real danger of losing his job.

While the rejig clearly had its intended effect on the Leeds defence – among the ever-present clubs in the division, only champions Arsenal, City and Nottingham Forest have conceded fewer goals since the switch – it has helped in other areas too.

The most notable beneficiary has been Dominic Calvert-Lewin. Since last December only Erling Haaland, Ollie Watkins and Joao Pedro have scored more top-flight goals than Calvert-Lewin's 14.

Having toiled as the lone centre-forward in a 4-3-3 formation, relying on infrequent support from out wide, Calvert-Lewin has thrived with a proper strike partner, often in the form of Nmecha or Okafor, who boasts seven goals and an assist in his past 11 league appearances.

Although Farke still finds himself alternating between 3-4-3 and 3-5-2, Calvert-Lewin himself has said: "I enjoy having bodies around me."

With Crystal Palace the visitors to Elland Road on Saturday, Calvert-Lewin is aiming to become the first Leeds player to score in six consecutive league home games since Arthur Hydes in 1932.

The former Everton forward missed out on a place in England's World Cup squad but, with three goals in all competitions this season, he is surely in with a chance of an international recall on Friday as Thomas Tuchel prepares for the Nations League quadruple-header.

Elland Road was bouncing on Monday night as the vast majority of the 36,693 fans savoured Leeds' stunning performance.

The famous old ground has been something of a fortress under the lights in recent seasons. Before consecutive losses to City and Sunderland in February, Leeds had gone 25 evening kick-offs in league and play-off games without a home defeat, winning 20 and drawing five.

The thumping win over Newcastle meant their new manager, Matthias Jaissle, became the latest coach to be welcomed to what Leeds fans call 'Daniel Farke Penitentiary'.

The online meme – in which managers defeated by Farke are 'sentenced' to time in his fictional prison – flooded social media again after the game.

Farke enjoyed the adulation of the supporters at full-time and, while he has quite rightly played down early talk of European qualification, a continuation of this form will have the Elland Road faithful dreaming of a return to those famous Champions League nights of a quarter of a century ago.

title: Eligibility rules 'not particularly fair' - O'Neill
description: Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill says what upsets him the most regarding rules over international eligibility is the pressure put on young players to make an irreversible choice.
fullText:
Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill said what upsets him the most regarding rules over international eligibility is the pressure put on young players to make an irreversible choice.

Any player born in Northern Ireland is also eligible to play for the Republic of Ireland, but Fifa rules state that an application to transfer international allegiance can only be made once.

The situation has again been in the spotlight with regards to Arsenal teenager Ceadach O'Neill who has won two senior caps for Northern Ireland and on Tuesday was included in the squad for a Nations League quadruple-header, but has also been subject to an approach from the Republic of Ireland.

At present, the player would be required to undertake a Fifa transfer of international allegiance should he wish to play for the Republic of Ireland at any level, but if he makes an appearance in the upcoming Nations League quadruple header, would have to wait until he is 21 to do so. Should he reach four caps, he would be unable to transfer at any stage.

"My focus is on the player, and I have a duty of care to the player as his international manager, as we have as an association as well," said Michael O'Neill.

"He's been in our pathway since he's been a young boy. He's been part of our academy. He's obviously had an approach from another association, which happens.

"The thing that upsets me the most in this is that putting a young player in a position to make an international transfer before he's been a professional for even two years is, I think, not the right thing. It's not something that any association should be doing."

O'Neill and Graham retain places in NI squad

Arsenal have 'big hopes' for O'Neill - Arteta

Under the Good Friday Agreement - the 1998 peace accord that followed the conflict colloquially known as The Troubles - those born in Northern Ireland can hold both British and Irish passports.

A Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling in 2010 means players born anywhere on the island of Ireland are able to represent the Republic of Ireland regardless of whether they fulfil any other measure of eligibility, namely being born in the territory, having a biological mother, father, grandmother or grandfather born in the territory, or having lived there for an uninterrupted period of five years.

Players born in the Republic of Ireland, however, cannot represent Northern Ireland unless they are otherwise eligible.

"We exploit eligibility, the same as every other country does, down to the grandparent rule, but this is a rule which is obviously unique between ourselves and the FAI [Football Association of Ireland]," said O'Neill.

"I think everyone recognises it's not particularly fair, but as I say, our focus is to make sure our pathway for our young players is as good as possible and that's a pathway for boys from any part of the community."

In May, FAI director of football John Martin said the organisation should at "the bare minimum" be sounding out eligible players.

"We know there are kids out there who want to play for Ireland who haven't been approached in the past," said Martin.

"That's not right. It's making sure we have a presence and we understand all the players available to us, and that they are being monitored and tracked."

When asked whether the narrative around young players in or around his squad is tiresome to him, O'Neill said: "It would have been in the past, it's not tiresome now.

"We have people who comment on this and talk about nationality and talk about identity and talk about all these different things, which are part of being born in Northern Ireland and growing up in Northern Ireland.

"But I think what we're missing now is that we're putting young players in a situation where they have to make a decision which is irreversible."

During O'Neill's time as manager, Tottenham Hotspur's Jamie Donley and Gillingham's Ronan Hale have made international transfers to Northern Ireland from England and the Republic of Ireland respectively.

"We've done two international transfers in my time. Jamie Donley, who is now a senior international, and Ronan Hale, who was 25 at the time when we asked him to make that decision," added O'Neill.

"I think there's a point in a player's career where you've just got to let him play and develop, enjoy his football without creating a situation like this.

"We haven't created this situation. Ceadach's been in our system all along and he's in our squad now."

While James McClean and Shane Duffy are the two most prominent examples of players who made the switch from Northern Ireland at underage level and went on to have long international careers for the Republic of Ireland, O'Neill believes others would have won considerably more caps for his side.

"I think if you look at it from our point of view, there's not many players that have been a success who have gone from Northern Ireland," he said.

"I can think of two, James McClean and Shane Duffy, who had international careers where they got over 50 caps. Otherwise, most of the other players who have gone that route have not played consistently or not had, I think, possibly the international career they could have had if they stayed here.

"It is a decision for the player to make, ultimately, and we have to respect that, but as I've said all along, I think there's two sides to this. There is obviously who you feel you should play for, but there's also the situation around a football decision where you can have longevity in your international career."

title: Celtic & Scotland legend McGrain diagnosed with Alzheimer's
description: Danny McGrain, described by Celtic as "Scotland's greatest-ever full-back", has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease, his family confirms.
fullText:
Danny McGrain, described by Celtic as "Scotland's greatest-ever full-back", has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease, his family has confirmed.

Speaking to the club's website, wife Laraine McGrain said she wanted to explain why the 76-year-old had become less involved with the Scottish champions and their fans.

"Danny received this diagnosis some time ago and, as time has moved on, we felt it was right to be open and clear," she said.

"Danny has always loved helping supporters - whether through hospital visits, assisting fans with charity events, or sending messages of support.

"As time has gone on, that has become more difficult for Danny, so we wanted to explain his situation with honesty and with the care and respect the Celtic family has always shown us."

Why does Sutton have 'great concerns' about Celtic?

McGregor laments Celtic's 'team of individuals'

McGrain, who played 62 times for Scotland, came through Celtic's youth ranks and spent 17 years with the Glasgow club.

He had one season with Hamilton Academical before ending his distinguished career in 1988 and going on to manage Arbroath for two seasons.

Celtic point out that he "remained a constant presence at Celtic over the years through a range of coaching roles, supporting our youth development programme via Celtic Pools and hosting hospitality at Celtic Park".

"In recent weeks, Laraine and their daughters, Vicki, Dawn and Carly, decided they wanted to be open with supporters so that Danny can continue to receive the love and support of the Celtic family, just as he has given so freely and humbly to others throughout his life," the club state.

"Despite the changes this diagnosis has brought, Danny remains in good spirits, enjoying time with his loved ones, following the game and staying close to the club he holds so dear."

As a player, McGrain became a Celtic legend, with the club pointing out that "he was widely considered by football experts, journalists, and peers to be the finest right-back in world football during the 1970s".

Overall, he played 663 games for Celtic between 1970 and 1987, winning seven League Championships, five Scottish Cups and two Scottish League Cups before helping Accies win promotion to the top flight in his final season.

title: McBurnie & seven uncapped players in Scotland squad
description: Hull City forward Oli McBurnie is called up to the Scotland squad for the first time in five years while seven uncapped make new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli's first selection.
fullText:
Oli McBurnie has been recalled to the Scotland squad for the first time in five years, with new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli also including seven uncapped players.

Luis Binks, Colby Donovan, Jon McCracken, Josh McPake and Stephen Welsh join McBurnie in Pocognoli's first selection for upcoming Nations League matches against Slovenia (home and away), North Macedonia, and Switzerland.

As expected, Stoke defender Luke Graham and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure also received their first senior call-ups.

Scott Bain, Kieron Bowie, Josh Doig, Lennon Miller and James Wilson are recalled, and Napoli midfielder Billy Gilmour returns after missing the World Cup injured.

McBurnie, 30, first featured for his country in 2018 and won the last of his 16 caps in 2021. He has never scored for Scotland but did net one of the penalties in the shootout that sealed a place at the delayed Euro 2020 finals.

He has long been out of favour with both Pocognoli's predecessor Steve Clarke and some sections of the Scotland support, but the new head coach said this was "a new journey" and that McBurnie fits how he wants to play.

The key talking points from Pocognoli's bold Scotland squad

Scotland fans allowed to buy alcohol at upcoming games

Is Sevilla's 'all-round striker' Ure ready to lead Scotland's attack?

"It's a new opportunity for some players, a really new beginning for the other ones," Pocognoli added. "I have to start a new journey, start a new book.

"The most important is regarding the style of play that I want to produce on the pitch. We need to adapt quick.

"To be honest, I can extend this list because I have to make some choices. There are a lot of names who can be also in that squad for that camp. Players who are not there is because for the style of play, it can be from injury or playing time.

"There's many players that I would like to call up. The door is never closed."

Pocognoli will take charge for the first time on Saturday, 26 September in Scotland's Nations League B opener in Slovenia.

He debut in the Hampden dugout will be three days later against Switzerland, with a trip to face North Macedonia on 3 October followed by the visit of Slovenia (6 October).

"We have a good mix between experienced players, new faces, first cap players, young lads, players who are back," the Belgian added.

"We have a lot of leaders, we have a lot of players who know how to win games.

"We want to be ambitious in this Nations League. We have to use this Nations League to try things, to experiment things but the most important is to be ambitious."

Binks, 25, has previously played age grade football for England and Scotland and Pocognoli said "the timing was right" to select the left-sided centre-back, who plays his club football in Denmark with Brondby.

Right-back Donovan, 20, has come to prominence with Celtic in recent months, filling in for injured Canada right-back Alistair Johnston ahead of Anthony Ralston.

Like McBurnie, he has been capped at under-19 and under-21 level. Pocognoli said Donovan had "played some good games" and had dealt with "expectation".

Graham was part of Scotland's pre-World Cup training camp in May after a breakthrough campaign with Dundee, winning the Scottish Premiership club's players' player and young player of the year awards.

The 22-year-old was an unused substitute in the send-off friendly win against Curacao, but moved to Stoke City in the summer and has started strongly in the English Championship.

Another new boy playing in that league is Swansea City defender Welsh, 26, who left Celtic in a permanent deal in the summer, having had a successful season on loan at Motherwell last term.

Former Rangers academy product Ure was in demand across Europe after his 20 goals in 20 matches took Sirius to the top of the table in Sweden.

That form resulted in a £5.5m summer transfer to Sevilla and, although the 22-year-old has yet to score in Spain, his eligibility for Ukraine made securing him for Scotland a priority.

Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken, was confident there would be a few players from the Tynecastle club included and winger McPake, 25, and 19-year-old attacking club-mate James Wilson, who has two caps, are recognised for their early-season performances. However, winger Calvin Miller misses out.

Bradford City keeper McCracken, 26, has been in squads previously, but has yet to win a cap. He joins Angus Gunn, Liam Kelly, and Scott Bain in the goalkeeping pool.

"I will not talk about my number one and number two today," Pocognoli said. "We have a strong generation in the past. Now we need just to rebirth this but we have good quality. We have experienced goalkeepers and we have some young talents."

Sassuolo forward Bowie, 23, and left-back Doig, 24, as well as Udinese midfielder Miller, 20, have also been recalled.

Fourteen of those named in Pocognoli's first squad were among the 28 players who went to this summer's World Cup.

Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay is unavailable as he recovers from a minor heart procedure.

Torino striker Che Adams is injured, while Rangers forward Lawrence Shankland is out for up to four months with a hamstring injury.

Gunn and Kelly; defenders Jack Hendry, Aaron Hickey, Scott McKenna, Nathan Patterson, Andy Robertson and Kieran Tierney; midfielders Ryan Christie, Lewis Ferguson, John McGinn and Kenny McLean; and forwards Findlay Curtis and Ben Gannon-Doak are all retained.

Goalkeeper Craig Gordon has retired, Grant Hanley has toiled with injury at Hibernian and Rangers defender John Souttar has not played this season.

Defenders Dominic Hyam and Ralston, midfielder Tyler Fletcher and forwards Lyndon Dykes, George Hirst and Ross Stewart also miss out.

When asked about the possibility of calling up Scotland-qualified Newcastle attacker Harvey Barnes and Everton midfielder Hayden Hackney, Pocognoli said he was "aware of everything and about the feeling of everybody" and said "it's about timing."

"I don't want to convince players," he explained. "They need to be open to representing in the natural way, the country. We'll see in the future."

Goalkeepers: Scott Bain (Falkirk), Angus Gunn (San Jose Earthquakes), Liam Kelly (Rangers), Jon McCracken (Bradford City)

Forwards: Kieron Bowie (Sassuolo), Findlay Curtis (Rangers), Ben Gannon-Doak (Bournemouth), Oli McBurnie (Hull City), Robbie Ure (Sevilla), James Wilson (Hearts).

title: Pidcock and Backstedt lead GB at Road Worlds
description: Great Britain's best cycling talents including Tom Pidcock and Zoe Backstedt will lead the charge at the Road World Championships - live on the BBC.
fullText:
Tom Pidcock and Zoe Backstedt will lead Great Britain's challenge at the 2026 Road World Championships.

The races for the coveted rainbow jerseys take place in Montreal, Canada, from 20-27 September, live across the BBC.

The championships include both the road race and time trial disciplines, with Pinarello Q36.5's Pidcock leading the men's team in the road race, while Ethan Hayter races in the men's time trial.

Lauren Dickson and Pfeiffer Georgi will likely lead the women's team in the road race and Zoe Backstedt will be expected to contend for the rainbow bands in the time trial.

Not for a long time have GB men a better chance to win in the road race, with double world champion and record-equalling five-time Tour de France winner Tadej Pogacar forced to sit out the rest of the season after suffering multiple injuries in a crash at the Vuelta a Espana.

Slovenian Pogacar has dominated the world road race for the past two years, winning in 2024 and 2025 to add to his numerous other honours.

The time trials come first in Montreal, with riders setting off at one-minute intervals, racing against the clock.

Backstedt steps up to the elite category after winning last year's Under-23 race and is joined by Anna Morris, 31, who has won a number of domestic races in 2026.

In the men's time trial Hayter, who came second in the opening time trial of the recent Vuelta a Espana, losing out to Pogacar by just nine hundredths of a second, will be joined by Callum Thornley, while the favourite will be defending champion Remco Evenepoel of Belgium.

Performance director for British Cycling Stephen Park said: "The Road World Championships are always one of the standout events in the cycling calendar, and we are excited to return with a highly competitive squad.

"This squad showcases the very best of British road racing, at a time when more British riders are making their mark across Europe and on the wider international stage than ever before.

"We're proud of the balance in this squad, from established world-class performers to riders taking the next step in their development."

title: Draper decides not to play again this season
description: Former world number four Jack Draper will not play again this season, but says he is aiming to return to the tour at the start of next year.
fullText:
Former world number four Jack Draper will not play again this season, but says he is aiming to return to the tour at the start of next year.

The 24-year-old has been suffering with bone bruising in his serving arm and has only played nine events since last year's Wimbledon.

Draper missed the US Open, after losing in the first round in Montreal and Cincinnati last month - and was in tears during his defeat to France's Terence Atmane in Canada.

"I am taking this time to reset and heal so when I return I am 100% ready to go," Draper posted on Instagram., external

"Tennis is my purpose and passion and so when I step back on court I want to make sure that there's nothing holding me back from where I want to go."

Why can't Draper play, and why won't surgery help?

Tearful Draper struggles during comeback defeat

Draper will not qualify for a protected ranking if he does return in January, as only those who are out for over six months are able to retain the ranking they had when they left the tour.

He is currently ranked 155, which means he would require wildcards or have to come through qualifying to play in Grand Slams and ATP Tour events.

But none of that will worry him if he is able to play freely and without so much pain.

Draper peaked at four in the world last June after winning a first Masters 1000 title in Indian Wells and finishing runner-up at another in Madrid.

"Last summer, all the dedication and work I had put into this sport was coming together," Draper added.

"It was all going my way and the path seemed so clear. However a complicated injury made things incredibly challenging, and since that moment I've been desperately trying to get back and feel as I once did on the court.

"Managing so much change, adversity and pain has helped me to grow massively in many areas of my life but has also made me feel a level of fatigue."

Draper has taken a holiday with friends in recent weeks and has been trying to aid his recovery by taking a mental break from the sport.

He is expected to make a gradual return to training over the next few weeks, as his team try to work out the principal causes of the injury.

Draper used to play with polyester strings, but has been experimenting with natural gut - which is against his instincts, but should ease the burden on his arm.

He has also started using a lighter racquet, and is making some changes to his serve. Diet is another area being examined to see if that, too, could be a contributing factor.

Andy Murray remains part of his coaching team but will do a limited number of weeks on the road, and so further assistance will be required.

Over the summer, Draper benefitted from the help of LTA coaches James Trotman (who was with him full-time as he rose into the world's top five) and Alex Lisiecki.

A permanent coach to work alongside Murray will need to be found, however, once Draper returns to the tour.

When he does, much thought will go into his schedule. Not just because the bone bruising is unlikely to have healed entirely by January, but also because of the concerns many top players have about the toll the modern game is putting on their bodies.

Liverpool confirm agreement to sign special midfielder
description: Liverpool have confirmed an agreement to sign an exciting midfielder. The midfield is a really tricky area for Andoni Iraola to figure out at the moment.It doesn't feel like he quite has the right pro...
fullText:
Liverpool have confirmed an agreement to sign an exciting midfielder.

The midfield is a really tricky area for Andoni Iraola to figure out at the moment.

It doesn't feel like he quite has the right profiles for his system to work. Looking at how Iraola used to play at Bournemouth, he had players capable of releasing the ball quickly.

At Liverpool, things are different.

And it's not just on the ball, where the Reds' midfielders struggle. The midfield is also porous. Gaps are too easy to exploit at the moment and it makes Liverpool's overall game ineffective.

That's why things need to change. Either Liverpool's current options start to perform or Iraola has to make some difficult decisions.

Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch both like to carry the ball, and neither are extremely strong when it comes to their reprise possession.

Playing the two of them in a double pivot just doesn't make a lot of sense.

Alexis Mac Allister is a much better players suited to the system and has also started the season in great form. In addition to that Trey Nyoni's ability on the ball also makes him an ideal fit.

However, if Liverpool want an intense ball-winner who is also capable of playing out from deep in the build-up, they will need to enter the transfer market.

Lamine Camara is high on the club's shortlist and a move for him would make a lot of sense. He absolutely could fix the Reds' midfield.

The Reds did sign a midfielder in the end.

Even though the transfer window shut two weeks ago, Liverpool quietly confirmed the arrival of Patrik Farkas as a free agent on the club's official website.

Farkas has returned to the club after leaving at U16 level to join Blackburn.

He has spent the summer training with the U21s and struck an agreement to join the Reds as revealed by Anfield Watch exclusively back in June.

Now the deal has been finalised at last, and the exciting U19 Hungary midfielder has completed his move to the Reds.

He sat on the bench for the U21s against West Ham on Monday night, and becomes the fifth Hungarian on the books at Liverpool joining his younger brother Erik, Armin Pecsi, Dominik Szoboszlai and Milos Kerkez.

title: Ausilio closing in on agreement with Tottenham after 28 years with Inter
description: Multiple outlets in Italy are reporting that former Inter director Piero Ausilio is closing in on an agreement to take over as the new sporting director at Premier League club Tottenham Hotspur after ...
fullText:
Multiple outlets in Italy are reporting that former Inter director Piero Ausilio is closing in on an agreement to take over as the new sporting director at Premier League club Tottenham Hotspur after his 28-year career with the Nerazzurri.

Ausilio officially left his position as sporting director at Inter on September 2, the day after the summer transfer window had come to an end and has since been replaced by his long-term deputy Dario Baccin.

MILAN, ITALY – MAY 17: (L-R) vice Sportif director Dario Baccin, director Piero Ausilio, President Giuseppe Marotta, coach Cristian Chivu and Vice President Javier Zanetti pose for a photo with the Coppa Campioni d'Italia and Coppa Italia trophies following the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and Hellas Verona FC at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on May 17, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Ausilio had originally joined Inter as a secretary with the youth teams all the way back in the late 1990s before progressing through various roles and eventually into the position of sporting director, a role that he held for well over a decade.

The Nerazzurri won three Serie A titles, three Coppa Italias and three trophies in the Supercoppa Italiana as well as reaching the Champions League final twice and the Europa League final once.

Reports over the weekend suggested that Ausilio had been approached by Tottenham to take over as sporting director following the end of his time in San Siro.

CAGLIARI, ITALY – AUGUST 28: Piero Ausilio sporting director of Inter looks on during the Serie A TIM match between Cagliari Calcio and FC Internazionale at Sardegna Arena on August 28, 2023 in Cagliari, Italy. (Photo by Enrico Locci/Getty Images)

Now, according to reports from various outlets in Italy including La Gazzetta dello Sport, Ausilio is closing in on an agreement with Tottenham. The Pink Papers claims that it is looking like a matter of 'when' and not 'if' Ausilio goes to Spurs.

He would find several Italian connections in North London, most obviously head coach Roberto De Zerbi and players Sandro Tonali and Destiny Udogie.

Ausilio would also be the second Italian sporting director at Tottenham following the tenure of Fabio Paratici, who is now at the helm at Fiorentina.

title: 'A tinge of disappointment' but Addicks are going well
description: Fan writer Paul Sullivan weighs up a disappointing game against Portsmouth with a solid start to Charlton Athletics' season.
fullText:
Two consecutive home 0-0 draws against Queens Park Rangers and Portsmouth have kept Charlton ticking over in the Championship.

I was very happy to take a battling point against QPR, who are recognised as a dangerous outfit and indeed dominated possession for long periods.

There was a tinge of disappointment at not defeating 17th-placed Pompey in a fledgling Championship table.

Charlton showed good fluidity in the first half and should have been rewarded, with Millenic Alli glaringly missing in front of the Portsmouth fans who were cheering him on last season but jeering this time.

Portsmouth emerged after the interval having absorbed and escaped Charlton's pressure, putting together quicker combinations and attacking the spaces more effectively. Their best chance fell to Abu Kamara, but Arthur Okonkwo went down well to his left to thwart him. Charlton regained control in the latter stages.

Very much like last season, we generally look sound defensively, but where are the goals coming from?

Three blanks on the spin, but you can also put a positive spin on that: just one defeat in our opening seven league games.

I'm sure all Charlton fans would have taken that when we were under starters' orders on August 15, and it has resulted in a sixth-place berth.

Away from the action, Nathan Jones has once again underlined his credentials as a stand-up comedian should he ever want to jack in the football job.

Jones himself provided the punchlines, joking that when he queried the disallowed goal v QPR, the assistant referee looked at him as if he had just volleyed his cat.

He also quipped after the Portsmouth game, that one of last season's shots seemed to have come from as far away as Blackheath, a couple of miles from Charlton - a memorable dig at Thomas Kaminski's goalkeeping.

Long may Jones remain our manager, and hopefully he is never tempted to return to God's Own Country if Mr Tan ever loses patience with Brian Barry-Murphy at Cardiff City, who are our next opponents.

There were one or two raised eyebrows when Jones was pipped to August's manager of the month award by Swansea City head coach Vitor Matos, following our maximum league haul. The Swans accrued two fewer points than Charlton.

Even perfection is not rewarded now.

So we journey from one Valley to several valleys on Saturday, hoping to avoid Cardiff taking their frustrations out on us by finally turning their plethora of missed chances into goals - and recording their first win of the season.

title: McBurnie & seven uncapped names in Scotland squad
description: Hull City forward Oli McBurnie is called up to the Scotland squad for the first time in five years while seven uncapped make new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli's first selection.
fullText:
Hull City forward Oli McBurnie has been called up to the Scotland squad for the first time in five years while uncapped Luis Binks, Colby Donovan, Jon McCracken, Josh McPake and Stephen Welsh also makes new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli's first selection.

As expected, Stoke City defender Luke Graham and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure receive their first senior call-ups.

Scott Bain, Josh Doig, Lennon Miller and James Wilson are all recalled.

McBurnie, 30, first featured for his country in 2018 and won the last of his 16 caps in 2021. He has never scored for Scotland but did net one of the penalties in the shootout that sealed a place at the delayed Euro 2020 finals.

Brondby's Binks, 25, has previously played age grade football for England and Scotland while fellow defender Donovan, 20, has come to prominence filling in for injured Canada right-back Alistair Johnston in Celtic's side this season. Like McBurnie, he has been capped at under-19 and under-21 level.

Graham was part of Scotland's pre-World Cup training camp in May after a breakthrough campaign with Dundee, winning the Scottish Premiership club's players' player and young player of the year awards.

The 22-year-old was an unused substitute in the country's send-off friendly win against Curacao, which was also Steve Clarke's last game in the dugout at Hampden Park.

The defender, who has three caps at under-21 level, has started strongly for The Potters in the Championship, who are unbeaten in their last four games, with Graham an ever-present.

Four-times capped Falkirk goalkeeper Bain and Bradford City keeper Jon McCracken were in squads named by Pocognoli's predecessor Steve Clarke.

Winger McPake and attacking club-mate James Wilson are recognised for their early-season performances at Hearts while Swansea City defender Stephen Welsh may also win his first cap.

Former Rangers academy product Ure was in demand across Europe after a free-scoring spell - 20 goals and three assists in 20 matches - that took Sirius to the top of the table in Sweden and it resulted in a £5.5m summer transfer to La Liga with Sevilla.

Time for Pocognoli to pick - who could be named in new-look Scotland squad?

Stoke best place for me to take step up - Graham

Is Sevilla's 'all-round striker' Ure ready to lead Scotland's attack?

Ure, also 22, has yet to find the target in Spain, but given his eligibility for Ukraine, the new head coach appears tempted to tie him down as soon as possible.

Since Poconogli was announced as Clarke's successor - the former Kilmarnock manager having resigned after the Scots failed to qualify for the knockout stages of a major tournament for the first time - the expectation was that the Belgian would look to freshen up an ageing squad.

His countryman, Heart of Midlothian head coach Wouter Vrancken, was "confident" there would be a few players from the Tynecastle club included.

His front three of striker James Wilson and wingers Calvin Miller and Josh McPake have been receiving plaudits for their recent performances but Miller misses out.

Former Scotland captain Scott Brown too had high hopes for the Hearts wingers, who have heavily contributed to their side's strong start to the season.

Pocognoli will take charge of Scotland for the first time on Saturday, 26 September in the Scots' Nations League B opener against Slovenia and his debut in the Hampden dugout will be three days later against Switzerland.

title: Roberto De Zerbi confirms Richarlison decision ahead of Liverpool clash
description: Tottenham Leave Richarlison Out Again Ahead of Liverpool Carabao Cup ClashTottenham travel to Anfield short on goals and without Richarlison, after Roberto De Zerbi confirmed the striker will again be...
fullText:
Tottenham travel to Anfield short on goals and without Richarlison, after Roberto De Zerbi confirmed the striker will again be left out for the Carabao Cup tie against Liverpool.

There is no ambiguity here. The player wants out, the club tried to move him on, nothing got done, and now he remains stuck between contracts, squads and plans. For Spurs, it is a poor place to be, particularly after back to back 0-0 draws against Nottingham Forest and Everton exposed a familiar problem in front of goal.

De Zerbi made it plain that the cup tie changes nothing. "Richarlison, you already know everything, nothing has changed for the Carabao Cup or Premier League. The situation is the same (he will not be involved)," De Zerbi said on Monday.

That tells you all you need to know. Richarlison was left out of Tottenham's Premier League squad earlier this month, and despite being eligible for the Carabao Cup, he still will not feature. This is a football decision shaped by a broken relationship.

Richarlison pushed to leave during the summer window and also rejected a contract extension. De Zerbi wanted to keep last season's top scorer, but there was never any appetite to force the issue if the player had already made up his mind.

Spurs then explored exits late in the window. Everton were part of that conversation, but a return stalled over personal terms. Similar problems emerged in talks with Trabzonspor and Vasco Da Gama. In short, interest existed, agreement did not.

The result is the worst outcome for everyone. Tottenham do not have the player available, Richarlison does not have the move he wanted, and the squad carries an avoidable distraction into a difficult game at Anfield.

De Zerbi did not try to dress it up. "I said last press conference, I know what happened in the last 45 days. It's not right if I explain. It's not my behaviour." He added, "It is the relationship and the problem is with the player and the club. I spoke with him many times to convince him to stay and he didn't want to. I can't go [about] every day to pray for him to stay."

That is blunt, and fair enough. Tottenham now need goals, with or without Richarlison. Liverpool away is no place for sentiment.

title: DeSean Jackson displeased with DSU's play as tough test at USF looms
description: Hornets weren't as polished as coach hoped in too-close win over Division II foe
fullText:
Coach DeSean Jackson felt his Delaware State football team may have overlooked last week's foe Division II Bowie State.

The Hornets still prevailed 21-6, though they weren't as dominant or proficient as Jackson had hoped.

DSU outgained Bowie State 391-287 in total yards and punted three times – once more than the visitors – but had drives stopped by an interception and two missed field goals. Bowie State possessed the football for 7½ minutes more than DSU while converting 7 of 14 third downs to the Hornets' 2 of 8.

"First and foremost, I'm happy about the win," Jackson said Sept. 14. "I'm just not impressed with the way we went out there and played.

"I just felt like there were a lot of things during that game that we kind of just shot ourselves in the foot."

Such self-inflicted wounds will be even costlier this week for the Hornets.

They'll visit FBS-level South Florida on Sept. 19 at 7 p.m. at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa. That's familiar ground for Jackson, who played two years there with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2017 and 2018 and made periodic visits with other NFL teams.

A LIFE TOO SHORT: DSU player's death from CTE inspires foundation to aid, educate

USF, a member of the American Conference, is 2-0 with wins over Florida International 19-9 and Army 28-24.

Delaware State improved to 2-1 with the win over Bowie State. That followed a win over Stony Brook and loss to William & Mary in which the Hornets had six turnovers but outgained the Tribe and had a fourth-quarter comeback thwarted.

Jackson hasn't yet seen this year's team develop the mindset or exhibit the execution that fueled last year's success in an 8-4 season.

"We're not in a position where we're good enough just to walk on the field and just think our talent is going to win football games," he said. "I told my team this is a very different team than we had last year.

"Year in and year out, you're gonna lose guys. Guys will graduate and you understand that. But the brand of football is gonna always remain the same."

That hasn't happened, however. The quarterback situation has also remained unresolved.

Troy transfer Ui Ale started the first two games but was relieved by William & Mary transfer Noah Brannock against the Tribe. He engineered DSU's rally in that game and started against Bowie State, but was then replaced by Ale in the second quarter.

Coastal Carolina transfer Samari Collier also saw QB duty against Stony Brook but has since been limited by a shoulder injury.

"We're just still trying to figure it out," Jackson said. "Consistency is a big thing and we just don't feel like we're as consistent as we need to be. No one's really took over that position . . . Those two [Ale and Brannock] right now are in a huge battle."

title: London loses out to Nairobi in bid to host 2029 World Athletics Championships
description: Nairobi, Kenya will be the first African host of athletics’ biggest event outside the Olympic Games
fullText:
London has lost out on hosting rights for the 2029 World Athletics Championships, with the event instead to be held in Africa for the first time.

Nairobi, Kenya submitted the winning bid, beating other candidate cities Rome, London and Munich for the rights to host athletics' biggest event outside the Olympic Games.

The hosts for the next two editions were announced in a World Athletics conference in Budapest, which has just hosted the inaugural Ultimate Championships, on Tuesday.

World Athletics president Seb Coe said "the interest in hosting our world championships has frankly never been higher" and praised "the quality, commitment and ambition demonstrated by all four... outstanding bids".

He said: "Taking our championships to Africa for the first time will be historic. Nairobi has presented a compelling and an emotional bid.

"This is a fast-growing, dynamic, modern metropolis that serves as the economic, cultural, and political hub of East Africa.

"Kenya is one of the great athletics nations. The sport is woven into the fabric of the country, and athletes such as world gold medallists Faith Kipyegon, Vivian Cheruiyot, Eliud Kipchoge, Hellen Obiri and David Rudisha, as well as two-time Olympic champion Kip Keino, multiple world cross-country champion Paul Tergat and multiple world half marathon champion Tegla Loroupe, have shaped the history of our sport.

"It was important that the World Athletics Championships should come to Africa when we had the right host, the right bid and the right circumstances. Nairobi has demonstrated emphatically that this is their moment to supercharge our sport, leaving a compelling legacy that inspires a continent."

Nairobi had submitted a bid for the 2025 edition but lost out to Tokyo, where it finished second in the medal table.

Munich was awarded host status for the 2031 edition of the biennial championships, which takes place in September at the end of the athletics season. It will be the third time Germany has hosted the event but first in the Bavarian capital.

Coe said: "Germany has proved time and again that it is an outstanding and dependable host for major athletics events. Berlin 2009 remains one of the memorable editions of the World Championships, and we have since seen tremendous support for the sport at the European Championships in Berlin and Munich."

However, the decision is a major blow to London, which had been seen as a frontrunner in the race. The UK government threw its weight behind the 2029 bid, with London Stadium - the arena purpose-built for the 2012 Olympics - intended to be the host venue.

But there were challenges even getting it off the ground in the form of needing to smooth relations with Championship football club West Ham, which had earlier argued it had priority to the stadium during the football season.

A deal was reached involving the London mayor's office, Athletic Ventures - a joint venture of UK bodies responsible for organising major events including the London Diamond League - and the Department for Culture, Media and Sport, which satisfied West Ham and meant the bid could go ahead. It was finally submitted last month.

But the public back-and-forth with the club was unlikely to inspire confidence in the World Athletics Council, while sparse crowds at the European Championships in Birmingham's Alexander Stadium this summer - despite being in a different city and in different circumstances - may also have damaged its standing.

Asked whether the West Ham saga played a role in London's failure, Coe refused to comment, saying: "I'm not going to maintain a running commentary today on the judgement and the basis of those judgements."

Jack Buckner, chief executive of UK Athletics and co-founder of Athletic Ventures, said: "We are deeply disappointed that the 2029 World Athletics Championships will not be held in London. We believed we had an outstanding bid which would genuinely take the sport to new levels.

"The UK is an incredible host for major sports events and the British public loves athletics. Athletic Ventures has the ambition to bring those events here and, although today's announcement hasn't gone our way, we will review and regroup. We know the world's athletes love competing here and we'll continue to explore further opportunities to make that happen.

"Our congratulations go to Nairobi and we wish the organising committee all the best for a great event in 2029."

London Stadium has not hosted an athletics championships since a highly successful 2017 edition, when Mo Farah won 10,000m gold and 5,000m silver and Britain took a surprise victory in the men's 4x100m relay. That event broke an eight-year record for ticket sales at a world championships, with more than 660,000 sold.

While the stadium has not hosted another major championships since 2017 it has welcomed the annual London Diamond League. A sellout crowd of 60,000 watched Scot Josh Kerr break the mile world record at this July's meet.

However that success was not enough to persuade World Athletics to choose the capital from the four candidates. London had specifically bid for the 2029 edition, while both Nairobi and Munich had indicated their willingness to host either in 2029 and 2031.

Beijing will host the next edition of the world championships, in 2027.

title: Squad tweaks show Morrison's 'trust'
description: Fan writer Jonny Drury dissects why West Bromwich Albion boss James Morrison embodies the concept of football being a 'squad game'.
fullText:
How many times do we hear the phrase from managers, "it's a squad game"?

They are right, it is, but managers very rarely apply that logic. They like to keep the same side for as long as they possibly can, depending on injuries.

We have seen it at Albion, certainly under Carlos Corberan when he had a slender squad, would hardly change things, and injuries would bite.

Flip that on its head and in the first handful of games of this season James Morrison has made a change in almost every single game.

In some outings there have been multiple, and some haven't always gone down well with the supporters.

Take the exclusion of Jimmy-Jay Morgan from the starting line-up against QPR for example. No one saw that coming.

Other key players have stepped out and then back in.

Some would argue that tinkering like that upsets the rhythm of the side, but it hasn't at all.

In fact, what it has outlined is that Morrison has something that a lot of other managers, who claim football is a 'squad game', don't have.

That is trust in all the players he has at his disposal. And that is a real positive as Albion try and kick on from a superb start to the campaign.

Players have come in and done a job, which in turn has seen Morrison develop trust in them.

There will be ups and downs, it won't always be this good. But for the first time in a while, Albion seem to have a capable squad who are all backed by the manager, and that can only be a good thing.

title: Cardiff to host 2029 women's Champions League final
description: Uefa have confirmed a number of host appointments for upcoming finals, with Cardiff's Principality Stadium set to host the 2029 women's Champions League final.
fullText:
Cardiff's Principality Stadium will host the women's Champions League final in 2029.

The 73,931-seater venue hosted the men's final between Real Madrid and Juventus in 2017 and will now welcome Europe's elite female talents later this decade.

"It's brilliant news for Cymru and the FAW and the journey that we're on, particularly in the women's game," said Football Association of Wales (FAW) chief executive Noel Mooney.

It comes nine years after Cardiff City Stadium hosted the women's Champions League final between Paris Saint-Germain and Lyon - with the latter winning on penalties following a goalless draw after extra-time.

The Cardiff city centre venue will be named National Stadium of Wales for the event to comply with Uefa sponsorship rules.

Mooney added: "This is about much more than one night in 2029. Our ambition is for the Uefa women's Champions League final to become a catalyst for the continued transformation of women's and girls' football in Wales."

Earlier this year, Principality Stadium - the largest stadium in Wales - hosted the FA Community Shield as reigning Premier League champions Arsenal won 3-0 against Manchester City.

"This is a hugely significant moment for women's sport in Wales and across Europe," said Welsh Rugby Union group chief executive Abi Tierney.

"We are absolutely delighted that our stadium has been selected to host the 2029 Uefa women's Champions League final, bringing one of the biggest occasions in world football to Cardiff and Wales.

"The rapid growth of women's sport continues to inspire new generations of athletes and supporters, and hosting an event of this magnitude at the National Stadium of Wales is a powerful statement about the importance and future of the women's game."

Uefa have also confirmed Munich will host the 2028 men's Champions League final with Barcelona staging the final a year later, 30 years on from Manchester United's dramatic triumph over Bayern Munich in the Spanish city.

The 2028 women's Champions League final will take place at Parc Olympic Lyonnais.

It has also been announced that the National Arena in Bucharest will host the 2028 Europa League final. The National Stadium in Belgrade will hold the Europa League final a year later.

Turin's iconic Juventus Stadium will host the 2028 Conference League final. The Puskss Arena in Budapest will host the 2029 showpiece.
